headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action exposure between gpt-researcher and Replit Agent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher can read files and use MCP, while Replit Agent can write the Repl filesystem and acts inside a persistent workspace. That creates a plausible bridge where content from one can be consumed by the other as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is not safely isolated.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher writes research output into a shared Repl workspace that Replit Agent later reads
IF either agent treats file contents as trusted instructions without provenance tagging
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for the two agents
Disable automatic ingestion of generated files as prompts
Add a provenance header to all inter-agent files
Require manual review before Replit Agent reads gpt-researcher outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher touches local documents, citations, and images and has broad network egress; Replit Agent touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration and also has broad egress. If they share a workspace or secrets-bearing files, either agent can expose sensitive material through outbound API calls. The blast radius includes secrets and code exfiltration.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same workspace or mounted files
IF secrets or local documents are present in files either agent can read
mitigations: Separate sensitive files into a workspace only one agent can access
Remove secrets from shared directories before running either agent
Restrict outbound network destinations for both agents
Run a quick audit for API keys and credentials in the workspace

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have overlapping filesystem write/read and broad network capabilities, and Replit Agent can modify git state while gpt-researcher can spawn subprocesses and install packages. In a shared repo or workspace, concurrent edits can overwrite each other or corrupt git history. The profiles do not show locking or coordination, so conflict risk is substantial.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or directory
IF either agent commits or rewrites files without external locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch or directory
Pause one agent while the other writes
Use a simple file lock or manual turn-taking
Review git diffs before any commit or merge

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher is explicitly a research/content-writing agent that produces reports and citations, and Replit Agent is a coding agent that can act on workspace state and deployments. If Replit Agent treats gpt-researcher output as authoritative, errors can cascade into code changes or deployment actions. No verification step is documented in either profile.
conditions: IF Replit Agent uses gpt-researcher reports as direct implementation input
IF no human or automated verification step checks the research output before action
mitigations: Require a human review of research outputs before coding
Add a checklist to verify citations and claims
Keep research notes separate from executable files
Block deployment actions until a second pass confirms the plan

E_compliance.rationale: Replit Agent handles secrets and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl, while gpt-researcher handles local documents and citations with broad egress. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch if regulated or residency-bound data is placed into the shared workflow. The profiles do not document matching retention or residency controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF regulated data such as customer records or secrets are routed through both agents
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the shared workspace
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair’s shared workflow
Document where files and secrets are stored
Delete temporary research artifacts after use
Confirm the workspace’s retention policy before processing sensitive data
